overview: Brent crude whipsawed on Monday, dropping toward $107 in early Asian trading after President Trump's executive order waiving sanctions on Russia raised the prospect of additional supply, before recovering to close near $109.55 — essentially flat on the day. The intraday reversal underscored the Strait of Hormuz as the dominant price driver: UKMTO logged at least 12 vessel attacks in the week ending October 16, including two ships struck by naval mines, and the M/V GFS Pride was sunk. Kpler measured crude flows at just 11.6 million barrels a day for the seven days to October 13, down from 12.6 million the prior week and about 68% of the 17.1 million pre-war baseline. Iran's crude exports have reportedly fallen to zero under a US naval blockade. Coal held near $150 at a three-year high.

Gold fell 0.6% to about $4,140 as risk appetite improved on China's better-than-expected Q3 GDP of 4.5%, while US Treasury yields edged higher with the 10-year above 5.1%. The Fed is in its communications blackout ahead of the October 27–28 FOMC meeting. Grains sold off sharply: December corn broke below $4.70 for the first time since August on harvest pressure, soybeans fell to $12.54, and wheat dropped to $6.55. Palladium slid further to $1,101, extending its monthly loss to about 15%. Bitcoin held near $83,000 ahead of a busy earnings week led by Tesla, Meta and IBM.

watchItems.title: Hormuz flows at 68% of baseline
watchItems.text: Crude flows fell to 11.6M b/d from 12.6M the prior week. Two vessels sunk, naval mines deployed, and Iran's exports reportedly at zero. Trump has reportedly ordered the military to prepare options for a wider response after the November 3 midterms.

watchItems.title: FOMC, Oct 27–28
watchItems.text: The Fed is in blackout. Markets see less than 20% chance of an October hike, but September CPI at 3.7% y/y and PPI at 6.3% y/y keep the door open. Statement language will drive gold, silver and rate-sensitive assets.

watchItems.title: Big-cap earnings: Tesla, Meta, IBM
watchItems.text: Tesla and Meta report Wednesday, IBM Tuesday. Results will test whether the Nasdaq's 4.5% prior-week decline was overdone. Energy costs are a key margin driver across sectors this quarter.

watchItems.title: US harvest pressure on grains
watchItems.text: Corn broke $4.70 support for the first time since August. The soybean harvest is running ahead of the five-year average and pointing to a record crop. Watch the next USDA crop progress report for pace and yield updates.

desk.name: Gold
desk.sum: Gold fell 0.6% to about $4,140 on Monday as risk sentiment improved after China posted Q3 GDP growth of 4.5%, beating the 4.4% consensus. US Treasury yields ticked higher with the 10-year above 5.1%, adding headwinds. The Fed is in its pre-FOMC blackout, with the October 27–28 meeting now expected to hold rates at 3.75–4.00%. Gold remains about 26% below its January record near $5,608.

desk.name: Silver
desk.sum: Silver edged up 0.2% to $56.97 on Monday, modestly outperforming gold as industrial demand provided support. The metal is still down nearly 14% on the month and about 53% below its late-January record near $121.6. The Silver Institute projects a sixth straight supply deficit this year, but higher Treasury yields and rate-hike uncertainty continue to cap rallies.

desk.name: Oil
desk.sum: Brent crude whipsawed on Monday, dropping toward $107 in early trading after Trump's Russia sanctions waiver before recovering to close near $109.55, essentially flat on the day. The intraday reversal highlighted Hormuz as the dominant driver: at least 12 vessels were attacked in the past week, two were sunk, and Kpler shows crude flows at just 11.6 million barrels a day — 68% of the pre-war baseline. Iran's exports have reportedly dropped to zero under a US naval blockade. WTI settled near $101.

desk.name: Copper
desk.sum: Copper firmed to $6.54 per pound on Monday, supported by China's better-than-expected Q3 GDP and ongoing supply disruptions in Chile. BHP reported a 19% drop in September-quarter copper output to 400,700 tonnes. The Comex premium over LME has narrowed as traders question whether US copper tariffs will proceed. The metal trades about 4.5% below its September record of $6.85.

desk.name: Coal
desk.sum: Newcastle coal held steady near $150.40 a tonne, close to a three-year high. LNG remains expensive due to Middle East disruption, keeping coal about 80% cheaper and supporting pre-winter stocking by Asian and European utilities. Indonesia's tightened export rules cut August shipments 23%, and an Australian court ruling blocking a NSW mine expansion is constraining supply further.

desk.name: Platinum
desk.sum: Platinum rose 0.6% to $1,635 on Monday, rebounding from a three-month low hit last week. Better China GDP data supported industrial demand expectations, though investment outflows persist and the WPIC expects total platinum demand to fall 18% this year. The metal remains about 8.8% below its September levels.

desk.name: Palladium
desk.sum: Palladium ticked up 0.5% to $1,101 but remains in a steep downtrend, now about 15% below its September levels and more than 25% lower on the year. EV adoption continues to erode catalytic-converter demand, and investment outflows show no sign of reversing. The Russia sanctions waiver could also ease tight palladium supply from Norilsk Nickel, adding a bearish overhang.

desk.name: Hormuz Terminal
desk.sum: The Strait of Hormuz crisis deepened in the second week of October. UKMTO logged at least 12 vessel attacks in the week ending October 16, including two ships struck by naval mines. The M/V GFS Pride sank and a supertanker carrying over two million barrels of crude caught fire. Kpler data shows crude flows at 11.6 million barrels a day for the seven days to October 13, down from 12.6 million the prior week and 68% of the 17.1 million pre-war baseline. Iran's crude exports have reportedly fallen to zero under the US naval blockade. Both the US and Iran claim control of the strait.

desk.name: Corn
desk.sum: December corn fell 7¼ cents to $4.67 on Monday, breaking below $4.70 for the first time since August. The USDA's yield estimate of 181.2 bushels per acre points to a large crop, and harvest pressure is intensifying. Fund liquidation has accelerated the decline, with corn now down about 14% on the month.

desk.name: Wheat
desk.sum: CBOT December wheat fell 5¼ cents to $6.55¼ on Monday, extending its recent decline. Winter wheat planting is progressing and weekly export sales fell to the bottom of analyst estimates the prior week, offering little demand support. Wheat remains about 31% higher on the year but is now 10% lower on the month.

desk.name: Soybean
desk.sum: November soybeans fell 7¾ cents to $12.53½ on Monday as harvest pressure weighed. The US soybean harvest is running ahead of the five-year average and pointing to a record crop. China booked additional December cargoes last week, but the pace of new buying has slowed and September crush hit a 13-month low, tempering demand expectations.

desk.name: Cryptocurrencies
desk.sum: Bitcoin climbed about 1% to near $83,000 on Monday, finding support from an improved equity tone after China's Q3 GDP beat forecasts. US spot bitcoin ETFs have seen about $617 million in net outflows in October through October 16. Ethereum edged up to about $2,429. Markets are watching this week's earnings from Tesla, Meta and IBM, along with Friday's final University of Michigan consumer sentiment report, for signals on risk appetite.
